prompt:
You are a junior associate at Wexford Strait & Akiyama LLP. Marcus Yeong, your supervising partner, has assigned you to draft a motion to dismiss in the employment dispute filed against our client, Meridian Partners, Inc. The complaint, which alleges violations of federal employment statutes, is attached for your reference.

Your task is to draft a complete motion to dismiss targeting all plausible grounds under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. The motion must analyze and incorporate the recent Fifth Circuit precedent in *United States v. Kimble*, 142 F.4th 308 (5th Cir. 2025), carefully distinguishing its criminal law context from the civil employment claims at issue. Structure the motion with standard sections: Introduction, Statement of Facts, Argument (with clear subheadings for each independent ground for dismissal), and Conclusion. Identify and argue at least two independent grounds, such as failure to state a claim or lack of subject matter jurisdiction.

The legal analysis must demonstrate a thorough understanding of *Kimble*’s holding regarding Second Amendment rights for convicted felons and frame its persuasive, but not binding, effect for the current forum. All legal citations must conform to Bluebook format, with proper pinpoint citations where relevant. Address potential counterarguments the plaintiff might raise and preemptively rebut them within the motion’s argument.

Prepare the draft in Microsoft Word format suitable for internal partner review, allowing for tracked changes. Include a certificate of service and ensure compliance with all relevant local court rules for formatting and page limits. The final deliverable must also include a proposed order granting the motion to dismiss as an appendix. The draft should be near-final and reflect advanced research and analytical rigor, ready for minimal revision.

rubric.criterion: Deliverable is provided as a single Microsoft Word (.docx) file.
File name follows firm document management protocol (e.g., includes client name, document type, draft number, and date).
Document is formatted for tracked changes (e.g., no final acceptance/rejection of all changes, and Track Changes is enabled in review settings).
Motion includes all required standard sections: Introduction, Statement of Facts, Argument (with subheadings for each ground), and Conclusion.
Proposed Order granting the motion to dismiss is included as an appendix to the motion.
Argument section contains clear subheadings for at least two independent grounds for dismissal.
A Certificate of Service is included at the end of the motion.
Motion complies with local federal court rules regarding page limits.
Motion uses a standard professional font (e.g., Times New Roman, 12 pt) and margins.
The tone is that of a persuasive legal brief suitable for a federal court, not an analytical memorandum.
Correctly identifies the client as Meridian Partners, Inc. in the caption and/or Statement of Facts.
Correctly identifies the supervising partner as Marcus Yeong.
Correctly identifies the firm as Wexford Strait & Akiyama LLP.
The precedent case citation is correctly formatted in Bluebook style as United States v. Kimble, 142 F.4th 308 (5th Cir. 2025) on first use.
The citation to Kimble includes a pinpoint citation to a specific page or paragraph where the holding is discussed.
The motion accurately summarizes the core holding of United States v. Kimble regarding Second Amendment rights and felony firearm possession.
The motion explicitly distinguishes Kimble's criminal law context (felon-in-possession) from the civil employment claims at issue.
The motion frames Kimble as persuasive, not binding, authority for the current forum.
First independent ground for dismissal is clearly articulated and legally viable (e.g., failure to state a claim under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6)).
Second independent ground for dismissal is clearly articulated and legally viable (e.g., lack of subject matter jurisdiction under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(1)).
Each ground for dismissal is supported by specific legal reasoning and citations to relevant Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.
Argument section addresses at least one plausible counterargument the plaintiff might raise.
The counterargument is preemptively rebutted with supporting analysis or authority.
Statement of Facts section accurately recites key procedural history (e.g., lawsuit filed, motion filed by defendant).
The motion references the assignment date of May 9, 2026, for internal tracking.
The motion references the internal deadline of May 14, 2026.
All statutory citations (e.g., 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(1) from Kimble) are in proper Bluebook format.
All citations to the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure are in proper Bluebook format.
The motion cites at least one other secondary source or precedent beyond Kimble to support a ground for dismissal.
The proposed order includes a standard "IT IS SO ORDERED" line and signature block for the judge.
The proposed order correctly identifies the parties (Meridian Partners, Inc. as Defendant).
The proposed order correctly references the case number placeholder.
The motion demonstrates thorough understanding of the persuasive effect of Fifth Circuit precedent in other circuits.
The argument for at least one ground for dismissal incorporates analysis of pleading standards (e.g., Twombly/Iqbal).
The Certificate of Service includes a placeholder date for service.
The motion includes a caption with the court name, case number placeholder, and party names.
The caption correctly identifies the plaintiff as the opposing party.
Legal analysis avoids unsupported conclusory statements; claims are backed by reasoning.
The motion is free of typographical errors and grammatical mistakes that impede comprehension.
Headings and subheadings are consistently formatted and clearly denote the structure of the argument.
The motion's length is appropriate and not unnecessarily verbose or repetitive.
The motion includes a signature line for the attorney (with name and bar number placeholder).
The motion correctly applies a relevant procedural rule (e.g., Rule 12(b)(6)) to the facts of the employment dispute.
The Statement of Facts is concise and focused only on facts relevant to the grounds for dismissal.
The argument effectively uses Kimble to analogize or distinguish the legal principles at issue.
The motion includes a table of contents or is structured such that sections are easily navigable.
Deliverable is submitted in a format other than .docx (e.g., PDF, Google Doc).
The motion fails to include the required proposed order as an appendix.
The motion identifies the wrong party as the client (e.g., not Meridian Partners, Inc.).
The citation to the precedent case is incorrect (e.g., wrong reporter, volume, page, or court).
The motion fails to identify or argue at least two independent grounds for dismissal.
